recommendation: Keep the fix as-is. It completes FHIR-35888 for the later-added Group compartment; any broader audit of Group compartment membership or CompartmentType terminology should be handled under FHIR-48863 follow-up or a new tracker.
issue_request: FHIR-35888 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 and asked whether a compartment's identity resource is in its own compartment. The approved resolution says a compartment implicitly always includes its root resource and rendered compartment content should include the resource itself.
initial_application: Git commit c2ddea7415c6952f2988e332315c5e1becdf9bd0 appears to have applied the issue by adding CompartmentDefinition Base Resource narrative, updating the compartment template, and changing Patient to {def} | link. The then-current Encounter, RelatedPerson, Practitioner, and Device rows already had {def} markers.
additional_context: FHIR-48863 later added a Group compartment and is already represented on the combined branch by commit 9608dfed9a86ec8e5c5b6ecf3e076a3efb026284. That later change left the Group resource row without a {def} marker in the Group compartment column, making the current matrix inconsistent with FHIR-35888. Group and CompartmentDefinition are active current resources in source/fhir.ini.
reconciliation: Changed source/compartments.xml to add {def} to the Group row's Group compartment column. The edit is limited to the root-resource marker and does not add Group.member as a Group-compartment inclusion rule, preserving FHIR-48863's boundary that Group members and resources linked only to members are not included.
source_changes: source/compartments.xml: added {def} to the Group resource row's Group compartment column.
